Punctual or change-of-state predicates in the identical frame (make, get, start, open, arrive, fall, grow, run, move, enter, escape, become, decide, write) leave it near zero, and the identity of the state complement does not matter (quiet vs silent gives the same peak), so it is not preparing the next token.

After a fourteen-month investigation, the state attorney general's office filed a sixty-three-page complaint on Tuesday against the owner of the Riverside Care Home, alleging that staff had falsified safety inspection logs and that administrators had ignored repeated warnings about a faulty furnace.

According to the complaint, inspectors visited the facility in March and again in June. They found that the boiler had been installed without a permit, that the fire exits on the second floor had been chained shut, and that the overnight staff on at least eleven occasions had failed to complete the required rounds. The report names three former employees, all of whom declined to comment when they were reached by telephone on Wednesday.

The owner's attorney, Marguerite Ellison, disputed the allegations in a statement, saying that the home had passed every state inspection for the past six years and that the missing log entries reflected a software migration that had begun in February and had not yet been completed. She added that the facility had retained an outside engineering firm to review the furnace and that the firm had recommended only minor repairs.

Residents' families described a different picture. A daughter of one eighty-four-year-old resident said that she had complained to the administrator in April and had received no reply for more than three months. Another family said that they had asked to see the inspection records and had been told that the files were stored off-site. Two of the residents have since moved to a facility across the county; a third arrived at the hospital on the night of the furnace failure and was treated for smoke inhalation.

The county prosecutor, meanwhile, has asked a judge to set bail at two hundred thousand dollars, arguing that the owner has substantial assets outside the state. At a hearing on Monday, the owner's lawyer asked for a postponement, which the judge denied. After the hearing, the owner remained in custody at the county jail while his lawyer prepared an appeal.

The complaint is the second filed against the company in five years. The first, settled in 2021, required the owner to hire an independent monitor and to report quarterly to the state. The monitor's reports, which are public, show that staffing levels fell below the required minimum in seven of the twelve quarters covered.

The care home, which employs roughly one hundred and forty people, sits on a six-acre lot near the interstate highway. It has not admitted a new resident since the complaint was filed, and state regulators have said they will decide next month whether to suspend its license.
